name: Elizabeth
overview: Elizabeth is a female member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the wife of Zacharias. Her identity is grounded in her Levitical lineage and her role within the biblical narrative as recorded in Luke 1:5. There are no additional notes provided that expand on her character beyond these facts.
namesAndTitles: The name Elizabeth means 'G-d is an oath' or 'G-d is my fill,' reflecting a deep spiritual significance tied to the Hebrew name El. This name is recorded in Luke 1:5 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Elizabeth is explicitly identified as the wife of Zacharias and a descendant of Aaron, establishing her Levitical priestly heritage. She is also inferred to be the mother of John, connecting her to the significant biblical figure John the Baptist.
scriptureSignificance: Elizabeth holds an important place in Scripture as a godly woman from the tribe of Levi who, through her marriage to Zacharias, is linked to the priestly line of Aaron. Her role as the mother of John the Baptist situates her in the unfolding of God's redemptive plan, preparing the way for the coming of Christ. Her story emphasizes faithfulness and God's faithfulness to His promises within the biblical narrative.
